englishSummary.headline: Windows client guidance changes how QUIC is controlled
englishSummary.summary: The documentation now directs administrators to keep browser QUIC enabled and use Custom Acquire with a cloud firewall Block rule for UDP 443. DNS over HTTPS must remain disabled for FQDN-based acquisition. QUIC acquisition and blocking are in preview and do not provide end-to-end QUIC forwarding.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Configure and link the traffic-acquisition and firewall policies, apply them through Conditional Access, and remove existing browser QUIC-disabling policies after verification.

englishSummary.summary: The guidance replaces browser-level QUIC disabling with Custom Acquire for UDP 443 and an enabled cloud firewall Block rule. It also adds verification steps using traffic logs and notes that QUIC acquisition and blocking are in preview, without end-to-end QUIC forwarding.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Admins using the previous approach should keep QUIC enabled, configure and apply the acquisition and firewall policies, and verify a logged Block decision and TCP fallback.

modifiedFiles.commitMessage: Use Custom Acquire and cloud firewall instead of disabling browser QUIC (#14776)

englishSummary.headline: QUIC troubleshooting now uses Custom Acquire and cloud firewall blocking
englishSummary.summary: The guidance changes from disabling browser QUIC to keeping it enabled, acquiring UDP 443 with Custom Acquire, and blocking matching traffic through cloud firewall. Administrators must verify acquisition, block decisions, TCP fallback, and the inspection certificate.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Update the relevant traffic-forwarding and cloud-firewall policies; the client health check may still report a QUIC failure until it is updated.
